native_mechanisms: The die-stone never resets between marks: one running state carries the callus of every prior fold (no re-initialisation, fully sequential chaining).

Each mark's weight is pressed into the stone's already-turned position rather than a clean face, so earlier marks bend how later marks land (input combined additively into the mutated state, then permuted again).

Only the stone's final seated number against the wooden keeps leaves the desk; all intermediate turns and residue (the faces marks never seat on) are swept away and discarded (wide state, narrow truncated output with a non-absorbing capacity).
core_technique: A sponge-style ARX hash: 384-bit state split into a 256-bit rate (a0..a3, the only words message blocks are added into) and a 128-bit capacity (c0,c1, never touched by input, mixed only by TIP), absorbed block-by-block through SipRound permutations with constant IVs plus length, finalised by extra TIP/TURN rounds and truncated to a single 64-bit XOR of the state — not FNV/xxHash multiply-xor-shift accumulation.
